evidence.activity: In-house architecture and design team designs the company's own fitness centers
evidence.quote: We also benefit from our in-house architecture and design expertise that allows us to create operationally efficient centers and a consistent feel across our centers.
evidence.section: Item 1 > Our Growth Strategies and Member Experience Initiatives > Flexible Asset-light Real Estate Model

creativity.criterion: level 1: design used only as a routine business input

evidence.activity: Life Time Foundation funds youth nutrition and youth movement programs in schools and communities
evidence.quote: Since 2010, the Life Time Foundation has provided more than $12 million in support to communities nationwide and positively impacted millions of children.
evidence.indicators: more than $12 million in support since 2010; millions of children

community.criterion: level 3: named, ongoing community investment program with dollar and reach figures

evidence.activity: Life Time Education, an internal certification, learning and development division for all team members
evidence.quote: LTE delivers certification, learning, education and development opportunities for all team members.
evidence.section: Item 1 > Human Capital > Development and Training

community.criterion: level 2: employee development of any size

evidence.activity: Life Time Academy, a licensed school that certifies entry-level fitness professionals for careers at Life Time or elsewhere in the industry
evidence.quote: LTA offers a certification for entry-level professionals to prepare for a career with Life Time or within the health, fitness and wellness industry.
evidence.section: Item 1 > Human Capital > Development and Training

community.criterion: level 2: specific current external skills program, limited disclosed reach

evidence.activity: Life Time Inclusion Council with ambassadors at each center works on inclusion and cultural competency
evidence.quote: Our Inclusion Council works through committees to identify and incubate areas for enhancing inclusion and cultural competency within our organization.
evidence.section: Item 1 > Human Capital > Inclusion at Life Time

cross_cultural.criterion: level 2: specific current internal inclusion program, no reach figures

evidence.activity: Employee resource groups open to all team members
evidence.quote: Further, team members are encouraged to find support and resources in one or more of our five employee resource groups, which are open to all team members.
evidence.section: Item 1 > Human Capital > Inclusion at Life Time

cross_cultural.criterion: level 2: employee networks with no membership figures

creativity.reason: Level 1: creative work appears only as a routine business input (in-house architecture and design of the company's own centers); the core business is fitness clubs, not creating or enabling creative work.

community.reason: Level 3: the named Life Time Foundation is a community investment program with dollar and reach figures (more than $12 million since 2010, millions of children), supported by employee development and an external certification academy.

cross_cultural.reason: Level 2: specific current internal practices (Inclusion Council and five employee resource groups) with no membership or reach figures.

entrepreneurship.reason: Level 1: rests on general language only (an 'entrepreneurial spirit' and the company's own innovation), with no specific service enabling founders or small businesses.

ai.notes: The Foundation's $12 million figure is cumulative since 2010, not annual. The Foundation's 2023 expansion into forestation and conservation is environmental and not scored. Life Time Academy is described inside team-member training, so whether outsiders enroll is not entirely clear, and no enrollment figures are given; it is tagged external_education at level 2 only, and Community level 3 rests on E2. Life Time Foundation and LTA are the only external activities; the rest of Community evidence is employee development. Kids Academy, swim lessons and kids camps are fee-based member services with no figures and were not scored separately. 'Charity Events' appears only as a table entry with no description. The 51,800 member events reflect member social activity, not external education. Traps excluded: 'state-of-the-art' equipment; 'studio performers' (fitness instructors, not artists); Experience Life and digital 'content' (health and fitness content in general, not described as creative work); 'entrepreneurial spirit'; 'accessibility laws' (regulatory compliance only); member demographics (income, education, age) are a disclosure, not inclusion activity; 'diversified portfolio' of centers. Life Time Work co-working is not described as serving founders or small businesses. Item 7 excerpts repeat Item 1 content and add no new qualifying activities.
